newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Dollar to lean on 1.7240 marks prop.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar to lean on 1.7240 marks prop.

text.p: The dollar is set to find short-term support around 1.7240 marks with its sights set on an eventual re-run at recent highs, technical analysts said.
However, the risk remains for further slippage to around 1.6950-1.70 marks before the U.S. currency gathers its strength for the next push higher, they warned.
"The U.S. unit...looks more and more in a short-term top-building process," said Dominique Corombelle, techical analyst at Generale Bank in Brussels.
Corombelle said the weekly chart could be read as a wedge pattern, and many uptrends had ended in wedges.

"Short term we see 1.7240-50 holding. A break of 1.73 will encourage us we're going to see 1.7380, but I don't think we'll have the power to take that out," said Ian Park, director at Capital Management in Zurich.
Dollar/mark hit a high of 1.7389 on April 28, its strongest level since February 1994.
The dollar was quoted at 1.7270/77 marks at 0748 GMT compared with late Friday's European level of 1.7294.
Dollar/yen was barely changed from its previous close and signs were it would stay that way, chartists said.
"Of all of them dollar/yen should have the most potential to rally. On a weekly and long-term basis it looks one of the best, but short term it's doing absolutely nothing," Park said.
The dollar is in the middle of a 126.00-127.50 yen consolidation range, analysts said. Support around 126.30 should hold dips for a retest of 127.00 and eventual break of 127.50.
Dollar/yen's recent high of 127.47 on May 1 represented a 55-month peak.
It was trading at 126.54/59 at 0801 GMT on Monday versus its previous close of 126.65.
